clinician.trajectory_summary: A 34-year-old Middle Eastern female presented with a month of excessive coughing, mild dyspnea, cough, and left-sided chest pain. Initial CXR revealed a 10cm x 8cm opacity in the left lower lobe, which a subsequent chest CT characterized as a simple pulmonary cyst. Given the patient's history from a livestock-herding region, Echinococcus was suspected. Due to the risk of spillage with CT-guided aspiration, a left lower lobe lobectomy was performed on hospital day 6. Post-surgical pathology of the clear cystic fluid confirmed Echinococcus, noting hooklets. The patient was discharged with Albendazole and recommended serial follow-up CXR for 10 years.
